cases.name: All 8 roles execute on standard review

context.diff: Added new login endpoint with session handling, password validation, and rate limiting

structural_checks: All 8 reviewer role headers are present in output
Each role section contains at least one finding or explicit observation
Roles appear in consistent order

input.prompt: /8eyes review src/api/users.ts which adds a new user CRUD endpoint

context.diff: New REST endpoint for user creation with email validation and database insert

structural_checks: Each role provides its own independent analysis without referencing other roles' findings
No role defers to another role's judgment
Verifier is the only role that synthesizes across other roles

cases.name: Role isolation - each role stays in domain

context.diff: New React dashboard component with data fetching, chart rendering, and role-based visibility

structural_checks: Security role focuses on auth/data exposure, not code style
Performance role focuses on rendering/data efficiency, not security
Accessibility role focuses on ARIA/keyboard/screen-reader, not performance
Test Writer focuses on test coverage, not documentation
Docs role focuses on documentation gaps, not test coverage

cases.name: Findings reference specific file and line numbers

context.diff: New payment processing function with Stripe integration, error handling, and logging

structural_checks: At least 3 findings reference specific file names
At least 2 findings reference specific line numbers or line ranges
Findings quote or reference actual code constructs (function names, variable names, patterns)

input.prompt: /8eyes review src/db/migrate.ts which adds a new database migration

context.diff: Migration adding user_sessions table with raw SQL, no rollback, and hardcoded timeout

structural_checks: Each finding includes a severity classification (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Info)
Critical or High severity used for missing rollback and hardcoded values
Severity ratings are justified with reasoning, not arbitrary

context.diff: Input sanitization utility using regex replacement, handling HTML, SQL, and shell input

structural_checks: Findings include specific code references or patterns as evidence
Security findings cite concrete attack vectors or bypass scenarios
Recommendations include actionable fix suggestions, not vague advice

context.diff: File upload endpoint accepting multipart form data, saving to disk with user-provided filename, no size limit, serves files back via direct path

structural_checks: Security role identifies path traversal / directory traversal vulnerability
Security role flags unrestricted file upload (size and type)
Security role identifies direct file serving as information disclosure risk
Findings reference specific OWASP categories or CWE identifiers where applicable
At least one finding rated Critical or High severity

context.diff: JWT token generation using HS256 with secret from environment variable, no expiration set, token stored in localStorage, no CSRF protection on token refresh endpoint

structural_checks: Security role flags missing token expiration as High/Critical
Security role identifies localStorage token storage as XSS risk
Security role flags missing CSRF protection on state-changing endpoint
Findings reference OWASP Top 10 categories (Broken Authentication, Security Misconfiguration)
Security role recommends specific mitigations (httpOnly cookies, token rotation, expiry)

cases.name: Skeptic challenges assumptions and design decisions

context.diff: Redis caching layer with no TTL defaults, no eviction policy, assumes Redis is always available, no fallback, catches all errors silently

structural_checks: Skeptic challenges the assumption that Redis is always available
Skeptic questions silent error swallowing as hiding failures
Skeptic raises missing TTL/eviction as unbounded memory growth risk
Skeptic asks pointed questions rather than just agreeing
Skeptic does not defer to other roles or rubber-stamp the implementation

cases.name: Skeptic refuses to rubber-stamp clean-looking code

context.diff: Well-formatted notification service with typed interfaces, async/await, proper error handling, but no retry logic, no idempotency, no dead letter queue, and tight coupling to a single provider

structural_checks: Skeptic identifies at least 2 architectural concerns despite clean formatting
Skeptic questions missing retry/idempotency for a notification system
Skeptic challenges single-provider coupling as a reliability risk
Skeptic distinguishes between code quality and design quality

cases.name: Verifier synthesizes all roles into coherent verdict

context.diff: Order processing endpoint with payment integration, inventory check, email notification, database transaction, but missing input validation and no rate limiting

structural_checks: Verifier section appears last, after all other roles
Verifier references findings from multiple other roles in its synthesis
Verifier provides a clear BLOCK or PASS verdict
Verdict includes justification citing the most critical findings
Verifier identifies the minimum changes required before re-review

cases.name: Verifier issues PASS with conditions when appropriate

context.diff: String formatting utility with proper input validation, typed parameters, comprehensive JSDoc, handles edge cases, but missing unit tests and one unused import

structural_checks: Verifier issues PASS verdict (not BLOCK) for low-severity-only findings
Verifier still notes conditions or follow-up items despite passing
Verifier distinguishes blocking issues from non-blocking recommendations
Test Writer role flags missing unit tests as a finding
Verdict acknowledges the low-risk nature while noting improvements

cases.name: Performance role identifies complexity and bottlenecks

context.diff: Fuzzy search implementation using nested loops over full dataset, string concatenation in hot path, no caching, regex compilation inside loop, synchronous file reads in request handler

structural_checks: Performance role identifies nested loop as O(n^2) or worse complexity
Performance role flags string concatenation in hot path
Performance role identifies regex compilation inside loop as avoidable overhead
Performance role flags synchronous file I/O in request handler as blocking
Performance role recommends specific optimizations (caching, precompilation, async I/O)
At least one finding includes complexity analysis notation

context.diff: OAuth2 implementation with PKCE flow, token storage, and callback handling

structural_checks: Only the Security role section is present in output
No other role headers appear (Implementer, Test Writer, Skeptic, Performance, Accessibility, Docs)
Verifier section is omitted or reduced to a single-role summary
Security analysis depth is at least as thorough as in full 8-role mode
Output is significantly shorter than a full 8-role review

cases.name: Graceful degradation when target has no changes

structural_checks: Skill handles empty diff gracefully without crashing or throwing errors
Output clearly communicates that no changes were detected for review
No fabricated findings are generated for nonexistent code changes
Suggests user verify the target or provide a valid diff
Does not produce full 8-role review output for empty input

cases.name: GLM 5.1 accepted as Implementer-alt or Test Writer-alt role

input.prompt: /8eyes review src/utils/parser.ts with --include-glm filling Implementer-alt role

context.diff: Pure-function string parser with no PII, no auth, no network I/O — touches only local in-memory data structures

structural_checks: GLM 5.1 is permitted as Implementer-alt role-fill on non-customer-data path
GLM 5.1 is permitted as Test Writer-alt role-fill on non-customer-data path
Vendor diversity preserved (GLM does not also fill Skeptic or Verifier in same review)
Recusal manifest entry for GLM is present and validates against schema v1.2

cases.validation_notes: Per /collab consensus 2026-05-01 Q1: GLM is allow-listed for Implementer-alt and Test Writer-alt roles only.

cases.name: GLM 5.1 hard-rejected from Security and Threat Modeler roles

input.prompt: /8eyes review src/auth/session.ts with --include-glm proposed for Security role

context.diff: Session token generation, refresh, and revocation logic with cookie handling

structural_checks: GLM 5.1 is HARD-REJECTED from Security role per consensus Q1 hard exclusion
GLM 5.1 is HARD-REJECTED from Threat Modeler role per consensus Q1 hard exclusion
Rejection cites the recusal manifest / hard-exclusion policy, not generic vendor preference
Reviewer fallback or substitution is proposed (e.g., reassign to Claude/Codex/Gemini)
Pipeline does not silently downgrade — rejection is surfaced to the user

cases.validation_notes: Per /collab consensus 2026-05-01 Q1: Security and Threat Modeler are hard-exclusion roles for GLM regardless of data path.

cases.name: GLM 5.1 hard-rejected on customer-data paths (T1 data classification)

input.prompt: /8eyes review src/vettara/customer_records.ts with --include-glm proposed for any role

context.diff: Customer-record query and write path for Vettara T1 customer data — touches PII and tenant boundaries

structural_checks: GLM 5.1 is HARD-REJECTED on T1 customer-data path regardless of proposed role
Rejection cites customer-data hard-exclusion policy (Vettara/Attestra T1)
Both Implementer-alt and Test Writer-alt assignments are blocked when data_classification=customer_data_t1
User-facing message explains the data-classification gate, not just role mismatch
Fallback to Claude/Codex/Gemini for the role is proposed

cases.validation_notes: Per /collab consensus 2026-05-01 Q1: T1 customer data (Vettara, Attestra) is a hard exclusion for GLM regardless of role.
